propositions: A stalled git fetch (connection accepted, zero bytes sent) hangs for the full 300s timeout instead of aborting quickly due to missing http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime configuration.
The fix adds throughput-keyed abort parameters (1000 B/s over 10s by default, overridable by env) to git subprocess calls so byte-starved connections abort in ~10s rather than wall-clock timeout.
Transient low-speed aborts are retried in-process a bounded number of times to self-heal within the same review, while non-low-speed failures (auth, bad ref) are not retried.
The git-subprocess and fetch-locking cluster is extracted from repo_snapshot.py (788/800 LOC) into a new sibling git_fetch.py module to satisfy the 800 LOC cap, with one-directional dependency.
